body.statement:
Let \(N=nm\) and \(d=|\mathcal G_n|\).  Under the predictable experiment class, polynomial family growth, and deterministic dense average-scale loadings, define
\[
 R_{g,\alpha}=2B\sqrt{\frac{\lVert g\rVert_F^2}{q}\log\!\frac{2d}{\alpha}}
 +\frac{2BC_\infty}{qN}\log\!\frac{2d}{\alpha}.
\]
Then, for every finite \(n,m\),
\[
 P\!\left(\tau_g\in[\widehat\tau_g-R_{g,\alpha},
 \widehat\tau_g+R_{g,\alpha}]\text{ for every }g\in\mathcal G_n\right)
 \ge1-\alpha.
\]
Uniformly in \(g\),
\[
 R_{g,\alpha}=O\!\left(
 B\sqrt{\frac{\log(2|\mathcal G_n|/\alpha)}{nmq}}
 +\frac{B\log(2|\mathcal G_n|/\alpha)}{qnm}\right).
\]
Thus the simultaneous stochastic radius has the separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) inflation and this factor is not part of \(b_{nm}\).  This conservative finite-sample result makes no claim that the frozen leave-one-cell-out multiplier critical value is asymptotically exact.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(N=nm\), \(d=|\mathcal G_n|\), and fix a deterministic \(g\in\mathcal G_n\).  By \(\mathrm{def:contrast\mbox{-}process}\), the definition of \(\tau_g\), and \(\mathrm{def:ipw\mbox{-}score}\),
\[
 \widehat\tau_g-\tau_g
 =\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J}g_{ij}
   \bigl(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}-M_{ij}\bigr)
 =\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J}g_{ij}E_{ij}.
\]
For the cell \((i,j)\), write \(\mathcal H_{ij}=\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).  The loading \(g\) is deterministic, and \(\mathrm{lem:ipw\mbox{-}identification}\) gives
\[
 E_P[g_{ij}E_{ij}\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]=0.
\]
Consequently the row-major sequence of summands in the preceding display is a scalar martingale-difference sequence.

We next derive deterministic bounds for its predictable quadratic variation and increments.  Consistency in the definition of \(Y\), followed by iterated conditional expectation and \(\mathrm{ass:sequential\mbox{-}randomization}\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\!\left[(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij})^2\mid\mathcal H_{ij}\right]
 &=E_P\!\left[
   \frac{A_{ij}Y_{ij}(1)^2}{p_{ij}^2}
   +\frac{(1-A_{ij})Y_{ij}(0)^2}{(1-p_{ij})^2}
   \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal H_{ij}\right]\\
 &=E_P\!\left[
   \frac{Y_{ij}(1)^2}{p_{ij}}
   +\frac{Y_{ij}(0)^2}{1-p_{ij}}
   \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal H_{ij}\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the denominators are strictly positive by \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\), and each \(p_{ij}\) is \(\mathcal H_{ij}\)-measurable by the definition of the recorded propensity.  Since \(M_{ij}\) is \(\mathcal H_{ij}\)-measurable and \(E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]=M_{ij}\),
\[
 E_P[E_{ij}^2\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]
 =E_P[(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij})^2\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]-M_{ij}^2
 \le \frac{2B^2}{q}.
\]
The last inequality uses \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\mbox{-}outcomes}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\).  The same two assumptions imply
\[
 |Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}|\le \frac{B}{q},
 \qquad
 |M_{ij}|\le
 |E_P[Y_{ij}(1)\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]|
 +|E_P[Y_{ij}(0)\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]|
 \le 2B,
\]
and hence, because \(q<1\),
\[
 |g_{ij}E_{ij}|
 \le \frac{3B}{q}|g_{ij}|
 \le R_g:=\frac{3BC_\infty}{qN},
\]
where the final inequality is \(\mathrm{ass:dense\mbox{-}loadings}\).  Therefore every partial predictable quadratic variation is bounded by its full-sum bound
\[
 \sum_{o(i,j)\le k}E_P[g_{ij}^2E_{ij}^2\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]
 \le \sigma_g^2:=\frac{2B^2}{q}\lVert g\rVert_F^2.
\]
The lower average-loading bound and \(B,q>0\) ensure \(\sigma_g^2>0\), as required for the stated form of Freedman's inequality.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:tropp\mbox{-}matrix\mbox{-}freedman}\) to the \(1\times1\) self-adjoint matrices formed by the partial sums, and apply it again to their negatives.  A union bound over the two signs yields, for every \(t\ge0\),
\[
 P\!\left(\left|\widehat\tau_g-\tau_g\right|\ge t\right)
 \le 2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2}{2(\sigma_g^2+R_gt/3)}\right\}.
\]
For \(x>0\), set
\[
 t_g(x)=\sqrt{2\sigma_g^2x}+\frac{2R_gx}{3}.
\]
Direct expansion gives
\[
 t_g(x)^2-2x\{\sigma_g^2+R_gt_g(x)/3\}
 =\frac{2R_gx}{3}\sqrt{2\sigma_g^2x}\ge0.
\]
Thus the preceding tail bound, together with the displayed values of \(\sigma_g^2\) and \(R_g\), implies
\[
 P\!\left(
 |\widehat\tau_g-\tau_g|>
 2B\sqrt{\frac{\lVert g\rVert_F^2}{q}x}
 +\frac{2BC_\infty}{qN}x
 \right)\le2e^{-x}.
\]

Take \(x=\log(2d/\alpha)>0\), which is valid because \(d\ge2\) by \(\mathrm{ass:polynomial\mbox{-}family}\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  A union bound over the fixed family \(\mathcal G_n\) has failure probability at most
\[
 2d\exp\{-\log(2d/\alpha)\}=\alpha.
\]
On the complementary event, \(|\widehat\tau_g-\tau_g|\le R_{g,\alpha}\) for every \(g\in\mathcal G_n\), which is exactly the asserted simultaneous inclusion.

Finally, \(\mathrm{ass:dense\mbox{-}loadings}\) also gives the uniform bound
\[
 \lVert g\rVert_F^2
 \le N\left(\frac{C_\infty}{N}\right)^2
 =\frac{C_\infty^2}{N}.
\]
Substitution into \(R_{g,\alpha}\), with \(N=nm\), proves uniformly in \(g\) that
\[
 R_{g,\alpha}
 =O\!\left(
 B\sqrt{\frac{\log(2|\mathcal G_n|/\alpha)}{nmq}}
 +\frac{B\log(2|\mathcal G_n|/\alpha)}{qnm}
 \right).
\]
The family size enters this direct finite-sample argument only through the union-bound value \(x=\log(2|\mathcal G_n|/\alpha)\).  In particular, the leading stochastic term has the separate factor \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\), whereas \(b_{nm}\) in \(\mathrm{def:frontier\mbox{-}rate}\) has no dependence on \(\mathcal G_n\).  No step uses \(\widehat s_g\), its positivity or consistency, or the multiplier critical value \(c_{1-\alpha}\); hence the result is a conservative direct-IPW band and does not assert feasible multiplier exactness.
